data.cultural_impact: The name Vibhavat holds a deep cultural significance for Hindus, as it evokes the idea of the divine presence or the manifestation of the divine in our lives. This name holds a positive connotation and is often used for individuals who are revered or held in high esteem within their communities.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Vibhavat is a powerful reminder of the divine nature of the universe and the interconnectedness of all beings. It encourages us to seek out the divine in our daily lives, recognizing that every experience and encounter contains a divine spark. By embodying the qualities of compassion, love, and service, as a spiritual ideal, Vibhavat inspires us to live in harmony with the divine will and to fulfill our dharma as committed seekers on the spiritual path.

historical_references.reference: King Vibhavatibhatta I (ruled 1231-1252 CE) of the Solanki dynasty in Gujarat, India, was an accomplished ruler and patron of the arts.

Vibhavatipura, also known as Vibhavatikonda or Vibhavatikonda Sivarama, was a hill fortress located in the present-day Andhra Pradesh, India, and was the capital city of the Eastern Chalukya Empire during the 11th century CE.
